products.note: Found in the research for The AI Ready School; not independently verified. AI: Model training. Use: Scratch-based machine learning projects. Who: Students, teachers. Student age: Not verified. Privacy: Not verified. Price: Free. Caution: Secondary source only.

reading.body:
Machine Learning for Kids is a free, independent, Scratch-based tool that lets students and teachers train models on text, pictures, numbers, or sounds.

The pattern here is a single product from a single independent project, not a company with a fleet of offerings. Its AI element is model training, which means students run the training step themselves rather than consuming a finished model. That places the compute on whatever device the classroom already has, and the data record says nothing about what that hardware is.

For AI specifically, the interesting fact is the audience. Students and teachers are being handed the training loop directly, which is the part of the pipeline that usually sits behind an API. The record does not say how much data or compute a classroom project consumes, so no claim can be made about whether this scales or what it costs to run.

What the data does not cover is substantial. Student age is not verified, privacy is not verified, and the source is secondary only, found in research for The AI Ready School. The price is listed as free, but nothing here confirms who pays for the underlying infrastructure. Treat this as a pointer to a project, not as a verified account of how it works.

profile_text.body:
Machine Learning for Kids is an independent project by Dale Lane, published at machinelearningforkids.co.uk. The site describes it as an educational tool for teaching kids about machine learning, letting them train a computer to recognise text, pictures, numbers, or sounds, and then make things with it in tools like Scratch.

The project is tracked as a product in the Education and Research AI category, with model training as its AI function and Scratch-based machine learning projects as its use. It is listed as free, aimed at students and teachers. The student age range and privacy practices are not verified, and the product was found in research for The AI Ready School rather than independently verified, so it rests on a secondary source.

No lawsuits, MCP servers, or other filings are recorded for this project.
